They have built on a large extension but there are hardly any doctors and the practice is poorly run.
Luckily we don't need doctors that often so have grappled through the difficulties of booking online and getting appointments. When we do need to see a doctor it's always something important.
However today after developing a urine infection over the weekend and waiting until Monday (today) to go to the surgery with a urine sample (obviously not normal!) so that he could get antibiotics, my husband was told the sample would have to be sent away! He was in pain and feeling increasingly worse. The receptionist said she didn't know how long it would take.
How can this be good practice? It's a simple dip test then antibiotics can be given straight away.
Urine infections don't go away on their own so we had to go to Urgent Care.
After 2 hours the doctor was seen and antibiotics prescribed.

I have also had numerous issues with medical requests not going through online, which is a problem and hopefully that can be fixed somehow! However, I understand that that is likely not their fault, and the doctors (special shout out to Dr Chu, Dr Sunassee, Dr Kansagra, and several others whose names I do not recall at the moment as I may have only seen them once; and to the nurses who have been wonderful with my kids; and to the reception staff who I can tell have been working incredibly hard and have done everything to help, including with more urgent manners).
